entities.summary:
Kaeso Duilius Longus was a Roman politician who played a pivotal role in the Second Decemvirate in 450 and 449 BC. He was a key figure in the governance of Rome during the late Roman Republic, serving as a member of the Decemvirate, a group of ten magistrates who governed Rome in conjunction with the Roman Senate. Longus's involvement in the Decemvirate had significant implications for the Roman Republic, as it marked a period of instability and power struggles between the Senate and the magistrates. This event had far-reaching consequences, including the eventual downfall of the Roman Republic and the rise of the Roman Empire. Longus's legacy also extends to his contributions to the development of Roman law and governance, which had a lasting impact on Western civilization. His name has been preserved through historical records and scholarly accounts, ensuring his enduring relevance in the study of Roman history. The significance of Kaeso Duilius Longus lies in his ability to navigate the complex web of Roman politics and influence the course of Roman history. His story serves as a testament to the enduring power of politics and governance in shaping the world we live in today.

The Second Decemvirate, in which Longus played a key role, was a period of significant upheaval in Roman politics. The Decemvirate was established in 450 and 449 BC, with Longus serving as one of its members. This period saw the rise of the Roman Republic's first elected representatives and the expansion of Roman power. The Decemvirate's influence extended beyond Rome, as it had significant implications for the governance of other Italian cities and the development of Roman law. The Decemvirate's legacy can be seen in the Roman Republic's subsequent governance structures and the development of Roman law, which had a lasting impact on Western civilization.
